## Step 1 — Define and resolve the workspace root, failing hard if it doesn't exist

Anchor everything to a single trusted root. If the workspace can't be resolved to an absolute path, abort immediately — never proceed on assumptions.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$workspace = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Projects\MyWorkspace' -ErrorAction Stop
$workspacePath = $workspace.Path.TrimEnd('\') + '\'
```

## Step 2 — Resolve the source directory and verify it exists and lives inside the workspace

Resolve the source with `-LiteralPath` (no wildcard interpretation). Then confirm the resolved absolute path is actually a child of the workspace using a strict prefix check — this prevents traversal tricks like `..\` escapes or a sibling directory whose name merely shares a prefix.

```powershell
$source = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Projects\MyWorkspace\data\olddir' -ErrorAction Stop
$sourcePath = $source.Path.TrimEnd('\') + '\'

if (-not $source.PSIsContainer) { throw "Source is not a directory: $($source.Path)" }
if (-not $sourcePath.StartsWith($workspacePath, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
    throw "Source escapes workspace: $($source.Path)"
}
```

## Step 3 — Resolve the destination parent and verify containment before computing the final target

Resolve the destination's *parent* first (the destination itself must not exist yet, or the move would nest or merge unexpectedly). Verify the parent is inside the workspace, then construct the final destination path and confirm it doesn't already exist.

```powershell
$destParent = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Projects\MyWorkspace\archive' -ErrorAction Stop
$destParentPath = $destParent.Path.TrimEnd('\') + '\'

if (-not $destParentPath.StartsWith($workspacePath, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
    throw "Destination parent escapes workspace: $($destParent.Path)"
}

$destPath = Join-Path $destParentPath (Split-Path $sourcePath -Leaf)
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath) { throw "Destination already exists: $destPath" }
```

## Step 4 — Pre-flight sanity checks (fail-closed guards before any mutation)

Because the operation is destructive if it goes wrong, validate everything *before* touching the filesystem:

```powershell
if ($destPath.StartsWith($sourcePath, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
    throw "Cannot move a directory into itself or its own subtree."
}
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sourcePath -PathType Container)) {
    throw "Source vanished between validation and move."
}
```

No unrelated files are touched at this point — nothing has been moved, and the plan only ever references the two explicitly named paths.

Perform the recursive move in a single `Move-Item` call (it recurses directories natively), using `-LiteralPath` on both sides so special characters like `[` `]` in names can't be misread as wildcards. Then verify the result; if verification fails, report loudly rather than silently continuing.

    Move-Item -LiteralPath $sourcePath -Destination $destPath -ErrorAction Stop
} catch {
    throw "Move failed, workspace left as-is: $_"
}

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath -PathType Container) -or
